# This is document for testing the function

This is an example of the Normal style used in a Microsoft Word
document. The normal paragraph style is typically used for the main body
text of a document. It provides the default font, spacing, and alignment
settings for regular content.

When rendering a Quarto document, this style is usually converted into
standard HTML paragraphs.You can use this section to evaluate
readability, spacing, margins, and text flow. This example helps verify
how content appears after conversion from Word to HTML.

# Heading 1

This section demonstrates content placed under a Heading 1 style. A
first-level heading is commonly used to define major sections within a
document.

When rendered through Quarto, it is typically converted to an HTML
\<h1\> element. You can inspect the font size, weight, spacing before
and after the heading, and hierarchy.

This placeholder text is intended to help assess the visual appearance
of the generated output.

## Heading 2

This section demonstrates content placed under a Heading 2 style. A
second-level heading is usually used for subsections within a larger
section.

When converting a Quarto document to HTML, this heading is generally
mapped to an \<h2\> element. Use this example to verify indentation,
font scaling, spacing rules, and style consistency.

The purpose of this text is to provide enough content to evaluate the
rendered design.

# Image Placement Instructions and bullet point example

-   Insert the image on an empty paragraph directly below this text.

-   The image must be anchored to the empty line so that its position
    remains fixed relative to the surrounding content.

-   Whe you click in the image you must see a little anchor with a lock

-   Set the text wrapping option to \"Top and Bottom\". This ensures
    that text appears above and below the image only, without flowing
    alongside it.

-   Center the image horizontally on the page.

-   Vertical: absolute position to parragrah.

-   Lock anchor and don't allow overlap.

-   Maintain the image aspect ratio when resizing.
